about.ex: The trip takes about an hour.

accept.en: to agree to take or allow
accept.ex: The union refused to accept the offer.

access.en: the chance or right to use something
access.ex: Everyone should have access to clean water.

according.ex: According to the report, prices fell last year.

achieved.ex: She achieved her goal of running a marathon.

achievements.ex: Winning the prize was her greatest achievement.

acute.ex: The hospital faces an acute shortage of nurses.

addition.en: in addition to: as well as
addition.ex: In addition to French, she speaks Italian.

adopted.en: formally accepted and started to use
adopted.ex: The council adopted the new plan last week.

example.en: Many doctors advocate free GP visits for all.
example.zh: 許多醫生提倡人人免費看家庭醫師。

note.meaning: （動詞）公開主張、提倡某做法；（名詞）倡導者。
note.usage: 動詞後直接接名詞或 V-ing（advocate reform / advocate doing），不加 for 較正式；名詞常見 an advocate for/of。

noteEn.meaning: To publicly support an idea or plan.
noteEn.usage: Use 'advocate something' or 'advocate doing'; noun: 'an advocate for'.

noteEs.exampleTr: Muchos médicos defienden visitas gratuitas al médico de cabecera para todos.
noteEs.meaning: Defender o promover públicamente una idea.
noteEs.usage: Va con sustantivo o -ing: advocate reform; como sustantivo: an advocate for.

noteHi.exampleTr: कई डॉक्टर सभी के लिए मुफ़्त GP मुलाक़ात का समर्थन करते हैं।
noteHi.meaning: किसी नीति या विचार का सार्वजनिक समर्थन करना।
noteHi.usage: सीधे संज्ञा या -ing के साथ: advocate reform; संज्ञा रूप: an advocate for।

noteJa.exampleTr: 多くの医師が全員の無料受診を提唱している。
noteJa.meaning: ある考えや政策を公に主張・提唱すること。
noteJa.usage: 目的語を直接とる：advocate reform。名詞は an advocate for。

noteKo.exampleTr: 많은 의사들이 모두를 위한 무료 일반의 진료를 주장한다.
noteKo.meaning: 어떤 정책이나 생각을 공개적으로 지지하고 주장하다.
noteKo.usage: 목적어를 바로 씀: advocate reform; 명사로는 an advocate for.

agreed.ex: The teachers agreed to change the timetable.

approximately.ex: The journey takes approximately two hours.

argued.en: gave reasons to show something is true
argued.ex: He argued that the plan was too expensive.

around.ex: Around fifty people came to the meeting.

as.en: in the same way; in the role of

asked.ex: She asked her boss for a day off.

aspiration.en: a hope or goal you want to achieve
aspiration.ex: Her aspiration is to become a surgeon.

example.en: Free healthcare should be a right, not an aspiration.
example.zh: 免費醫療應是權利，而非只是願望。

note.meaning: 抱負、願望；希望達成的目標。
note.usage: 可數名詞，常用複數；文中 mere aspiration 指「只是空泛的願望」，與具法律效力的權利對比。

noteEn.meaning: A strong hope or goal you want to reach.
noteEn.usage: Countable; 'a mere aspiration' means only a hope, not real.

noteEs.exampleTr: La sanidad gratuita debería ser un derecho, no una aspiración.
noteEs.meaning: Deseo o meta que se quiere alcanzar.
noteEs.usage: Sustantivo contable; mere aspiration = solo un deseo.

noteHi.exampleTr: मुफ़्त स्वास्थ्य सेवा एक अधिकार होनी चाहिए, केवल आकांक्षा नहीं।
noteHi.meaning: आकांक्षा; कोई लक्ष्य जिसे पाने की इच्छा हो।
noteHi.usage: गणनीय संज्ञा; mere aspiration का अर्थ है 'सिर्फ एक इच्छा'।

noteJa.exampleTr: 無料の医療は単なる願望ではなく権利であるべきだ。
noteJa.meaning: 達成したい願望や目標。
noteJa.usage: 可算名詞。mere aspiration は「単なる願望」。

noteKo.exampleTr: 무상 의료는 단순한 바람이 아니라 권리여야 한다.
noteKo.usage: 가산 명사; mere aspiration은 '단지 바람일 뿐'이라는 뜻.

available.en: able to be used or obtained

be.ex: Try to be on time tomorrow.

been.ex: It has been a busy week.

beneficial.en: having a good or helpful effect
beneficial.ex: Regular exercise is beneficial to your health.

between.en: in the space or time separating two things

big.ex: It was a big decision for the family.

branded.ex: Critics branded the new law unfair.

buy.ex: I want to buy a new jacket.

called.ex: He called for a change in the law.

cannot.ex: You cannot park here after six.

care.en: help and treatment for sick people
care.ex: The hospital gives excellent care to children.

cause.en: a reason for a feeling or action
cause.ex: There is no cause for alarm.

certain.ex: We need a more certain timetable for the work.

chair.en: the person in charge of a meeting or committee
chair.ex: She was elected chair of the board.

chairs.en: leads a committee or meeting as its chair
chairs.ex: She chairs the school parents’ committee.

changes.ex: The new law brought many changes.

characterised.en: described something as having a certain quality
characterised.ex: Critics characterised the film as slow but beautiful.

charge.ex: Delivery is free of charge for members.

claim.en: say you have achieved or own something
claim.ex: The team can claim a big victory this season.

co-founder.en: one of the people who started an organisation
co-founder.ex: He is the co-founder of a small tech company.

college.ex: She studies history at a local college.
college.ja: カレッジ（Trinity College：トリニティ・カレッジ）
college.zh: 學院（Trinity College：都柏林三一學院）

committee.en: a group chosen to do a task
committee.ex: The committee will decide next week.

common.en: happening often; found in many places

commonplace.en: happening so often it is no longer surprising
commonplace.ex: Mobile phones are now commonplace in schools.

example.en: Working from home has become commonplace.
example.zh: 在家工作已變得司空見慣。

note.meaning: 非常普遍、司空見慣，不再令人驚訝。
note.usage: 作形容詞多放在 be/become/remain 之後；也可作名詞指「平常事」。帶有「本不該如此普遍」的語氣。

noteEn.meaning: So common that it no longer surprises anyone.

noteEs.exampleTr: Trabajar desde casa se ha vuelto algo habitual.
noteEs.meaning: Tan habitual que ya no sorprende.
noteEs.usage: Suele ir tras become/remain: become commonplace.

noteHi.exampleTr: घर से काम करना अब आम बात हो गई है।
noteHi.meaning: इतना आम कि अब हैरानी नहीं होती।
noteHi.usage: अक्सर become/remain के बाद आता है: become commonplace।

noteJa.exampleTr: 在宅勤務はありふれたものになった。
noteJa.meaning: ありふれていて、もう驚かれないこと。
noteJa.usage: become/remain の後によく使う：become commonplace。

noteKo.meaning: 너무 흔해서 더 이상 놀랍지 않은.
noteKo.usage: become/remain 뒤에 자주 쓰임: become commonplace.

compelled.en: forced or feeling you must do something
compelled.ex: She felt compelled to tell the truth.

example.en: The storm compelled us to cancel the trip.
example.zh: 暴風雨迫使我們取消旅行。

note.usage: 常用 compel sb to do sth，或被動 be/feel compelled to do，表示因壓力或需要而不得不做。

noteEn.meaning: To force someone to do something.
noteEn.usage: Use 'compel someone to do' or 'feel compelled to do'.

noteEs.exampleTr: La tormenta nos obligó a cancelar el viaje.
noteEs.meaning: Obligar a alguien a hacer algo.
noteEs.usage: Se usa compel sb to do o feel compelled to do.

noteHi.exampleTr: तूफ़ान ने हमें यात्रा रद्द करने के लिए मजबूर किया।
noteHi.meaning: किसी को कुछ करने के लिए मजबूर करना।
noteHi.usage: compel sb to do या feel compelled to do के रूप में प्रयोग।

noteJa.exampleTr: 嵐のせいで私たちは旅行を中止せざるを得なかった。
noteJa.meaning: 人に無理に何かをさせること。
noteJa.usage: compel sb to do / feel compelled to do の形で使う。

noteKo.exampleTr: 폭풍 때문에 우리는 여행을 취소할 수밖에 없었다.
noteKo.usage: compel sb to do 또는 feel compelled to do 형태로 쓰임.

complex.en: having many connected parts; hard to understand
complex.ex: The tax system is very complex.

complicated.en: difficult to understand or deal with
complicated.ex: The instructions were too complicated to follow.

concurred.ex: The judges concurred with the decision.

consequently.ex: It rained heavily; consequently, the match was cancelled.

considerably.ex: Prices are considerably higher in the city.

convoluted.en: very complicated and difficult to follow
convoluted.ex: The film's plot was too convoluted for me.

example.en: The application process is long and convoluted.

note.meaning: 極為複雜、繞來繞去而難以理解。
note.usage: 多形容制度、論點、規則或情節，帶負面語氣，比 complicated 更正式、更強烈。

noteEn.meaning: Very complicated and hard to follow.
noteEn.usage: Used for systems, arguments or rules, in a negative way.

noteEs.exampleTr: El proceso de solicitud es largo y enrevesado.
noteEs.meaning: Muy complicado y difícil de seguir.
noteEs.usage: Se usa con sistemas, argumentos o reglas; tono negativo.

noteHi.exampleTr: आवेदन प्रक्रिया लंबी और उलझी हुई है।
noteHi.meaning: बहुत उलझा हुआ और समझने में कठिन।
noteHi.usage: व्यवस्था, तर्क या नियमों के लिए नकारात्मक अर्थ में प्रयोग।

noteJa.exampleTr: 申請の手続きは長くて入り組んでいる。
noteJa.meaning: 非常に複雑で分かりにくい。
noteJa.usage: 制度・議論・規則などに否定的に使う。

noteKo.usage: 제도, 논리, 규칙 등에 부정적으로 쓰임.

costs.ex: The cost of living keeps rising.

country.ex: Ireland is a small country with a big diaspora.

deliver.ex: Solar panels deliver power to the village.

described.ex: He described the hotel as quiet and clean.

did.ex: Our team did well in the final.

distant.ex: Peace still seems a distant dream.

dividends.ex: Hard work in school pays dividends later.

doctor.en: a person trained to treat sick people
doctor.ex: I need to see a doctor about my cough.

doctors.ex: You should see a doctor about that cough.

does.ex: He does his homework after dinner.
does.zh: 做；進行（does a survey：做調查）

dr.en: short for Doctor, used before a name

echoed.en: repeated or agreed with someone's view
echoed.ex: Many parents echoed the teacher's worries.

either.ex: I don't like coffee, and she doesn't either.

enshrining.en: making a right officially protected, e.g. in law
enshrining.ex: The constitution enshrines freedom of speech.

example.en: The right to education is enshrined in law.
example.zh: 受教育的權利已明訂於法律中。

note.meaning: 將權利或原則正式寫入（法律、憲法）而加以保障。
note.usage: 常用 enshrine sth in law/the constitution，或被動 be enshrined in。

noteEn.meaning: To officially protect a right by writing it into law.
noteEn.usage: Use 'enshrine something in law' or 'be enshrined in'.

noteEs.exampleTr: El derecho a la educación está consagrado en la ley.
noteEs.meaning: Consagrar un derecho o principio en la ley o la constitución.
noteEs.usage: Se usa enshrine sth in law o be enshrined in.

noteHi.exampleTr: शिक्षा का अधिकार कानून में सुनिश्चित है।
noteHi.meaning: किसी अधिकार को कानून या संविधान में पक्का करना।
noteHi.usage: enshrine sth in law या be enshrined in के रूप में।

noteJa.exampleTr: 教育を受ける権利は法律で保障されている。
noteJa.meaning: 権利や原則を法律・憲法に正式に定めること。
noteJa.usage: enshrine sth in law / be enshrined in の形で使う。

noteKo.usage: enshrine sth in law 또는 be enshrined in 형태로 쓰임.

entanglement.ex: The entanglement of politics and business worries voters.

entire.ex: The entire village came to the festival.

entitlement.en: a legal right to have or receive something
entitlement.ex: Holiday pay is an entitlement for all workers.

example.en: Every child has an entitlement to free education.
example.zh: 每個孩子都有權享受免費教育。

note.meaning: （依法或規定）享有某物的權利或資格。
note.usage: 常用 entitlement to sth；legal/statutory entitlement 強調法律保障；也可指「自認應得」的心態（貶義）。

noteEn.meaning: A legal right to have or receive something.
noteEn.usage: Use 'entitlement to something'; 'legal entitlement' stresses law.

noteEs.exampleTr: Todo niño tiene derecho a la educación gratuita.
noteEs.usage: Se usa entitlement to sth; legal entitlement subraya la protección legal.

noteHi.exampleTr: हर बच्चे को मुफ़्त शिक्षा का अधिकार है।
noteHi.meaning: किसी चीज़ को पाने का कानूनी अधिकार।
noteHi.usage: entitlement to sth के रूप में; legal entitlement कानूनी अधिकार पर ज़ोर देता है।

noteJa.exampleTr: すべての子どもには無償教育を受ける権利がある。
noteJa.meaning: 法律などで認められた受ける権利。
noteJa.usage: entitlement to sth の形。legal entitlement は法的保障を強調。

noteKo.exampleTr: 모든 아이는 무상 교육을 받을 권리가 있다.
noteKo.meaning: 법이나 규정에 따라 무엇을 받을 권리.
noteKo.usage: entitlement to sth 형태; legal entitlement는 법적 보장을 강조.

establishing.en: officially setting up or creating something
establishing.ex: The law established a minimum wage.

evidence.en: something that shows a thing is true
evidence.ex: The new jobs are evidence that the town is growing.

extended.ex: They extended the bus route to the airport.

faltered.en: lost strength and stopped making progress
faltered.ex: The economy faltered after the crisis.

example.en: Support for the plan began to falter.
example.zh: 對該計畫的支持開始動搖。

note.meaning: 動搖、衰退，失去力量或停止進展。
note.usage: 可指計畫、經濟、改革停滯，也可指聲音或腳步顫抖；常見 begin to falter。

noteEn.meaning: To lose strength or stop making progress.
noteEn.usage: Used for plans, economies or reforms; 'begin to falter'.

noteEs.exampleTr: El apoyo al plan empezó a flaquear.
noteEs.meaning: Perder fuerza o dejar de avanzar.
noteEs.usage: Se usa con planes, economía o reformas; begin to falter es común.

noteHi.exampleTr: योजना के लिए समर्थन कमज़ोर पड़ने लगा।
noteHi.meaning: कमज़ोर पड़ना या आगे न बढ़ पाना।
noteHi.usage: योजना, अर्थव्यवस्था या सुधार के लिए; begin to falter आम है।

noteJa.exampleTr: その計画への支持は揺らぎ始めた。
noteJa.meaning: 勢いを失い、進まなくなる。
noteJa.usage: 計画・経済・改革などに使い、begin to falter がよく使われる。

noteKo.exampleTr: 그 계획에 대한 지지가 흔들리기 시작했다.
noteKo.usage: 계획, 경제, 개혁 등에 쓰이며 begin to falter가 흔함.

family.ex: She lives with her family in Cork.

far.ex: This is far better than the old version.
far.ja: はるかに（far from：決して〜ない）
syn: a lot (far from: not at all)

feel.ex: I feel we should leave early.

feels.ex: She feels the plan is too risky.

flagship.ex: The store is the brand's flagship shop in London.

free.ex: The change will free up hospital beds.

furthermore.ex: The flat is cheap; furthermore, it is central.

gp.en: a family doctor who treats general illnesses
gp.ex: I made an appointment with my GP.

gps.ex: Many GPs are busy in winter.

group.en: a number of people or things together
group.ex: A group of students visited the museum.

had.en: possessed; was involved (had a hand in)
had.ex: She had a key role in the project.

has.en: owns or holds; also forms perfect tense

have.ja: 持つ；〜しなければならない

health.ex: The health service is under pressure.

healthcare.ex: She wants a career in healthcare.

heard.ex: The court heard evidence from three witnesses.

hospital.ex: She was taken to hospital after the fall.

hospitals.en: places where sick people are treated
hospitals.ex: Hospitals are very busy in winter.

individuals.ex: The service helps individuals find work.

inefficient.ex: The old heating system is very inefficient.

inequitable.en: unfair because people are not treated equally
inequitable.ex: The tax system is inequitable to poor families.

example.en: The current funding model is deeply inequitable.
example.zh: 目前的資金模式極不公平。

note.usage: 正式用語，多形容制度、政策或資源分配；名詞為 inequity，反義詞 equitable。

noteEn.meaning: Unfair because people are not treated equally.
noteEn.usage: Formal; used for systems, policies and sharing resources.

noteEs.exampleTr: El modelo actual de financiación es profundamente injusto.
noteEs.meaning: Injusto porque no trata a todos por igual.
noteEs.usage: Palabra formal para sistemas, políticas o reparto de recursos.

noteHi.exampleTr: वर्तमान वित्त पोषण मॉडल बहुत अनुचित है।
noteHi.meaning: अनुचित, सबके साथ बराबर व्यवहार न करने वाला।
noteHi.usage: औपचारिक शब्द; व्यवस्था, नीति या संसाधनों के बँटवारे के लिए।

noteJa.exampleTr: 現在の資金モデルは非常に不公平だ。
noteJa.usage: 制度・政策・資源配分に使う硬い語。

noteKo.usage: 제도, 정책, 자원 분배에 쓰는 격식어.

insurance.en: paying to be protected from loss

investment.en: money put in to get results

lacks.ex: The town lacks a good public library.

languishing.en: staying in a bad situation for a long time
languishing.ex: Many asylum seekers languish in camps for years.

example.en: Thousands of patients languish on waiting lists for months.
example.zh: 數千名病人在候診名單上苦等好幾個月。

note.meaning: 長期處於困境或被忽視的狀態而得不到改善。
note.usage: 常接 in/on + 地點或狀態，如 languish in prison、languish on a waiting list；多用進行式強調持續受苦。

noteEn.meaning: To stay in a bad or neglected situation for a long time.
noteEn.usage: Often used with in/on: languish in prison, on a list.

noteEs.exampleTr: Miles de pacientes languidecen en listas de espera durante meses.
noteEs.meaning: Permanecer mucho tiempo en una situación mala o de abandono.
noteEs.usage: Suele ir con in/on: languish in prison, languish on a waiting list.

noteHi.exampleTr: हज़ारों मरीज़ महीनों तक प्रतीक्षा सूची में पड़े रहते हैं।
noteHi.meaning: लंबे समय तक किसी बुरी स्थिति में फँसे रहना।
noteHi.usage: अक्सर in/on के साथ: languish in prison, languish on a waiting list।

noteJa.exampleTr: 何千人もの患者が何か月も待機リストで待たされている。
noteJa.meaning: 悪い状況に長い間放置されること。
noteJa.usage: in/on と共に使う：languish in prison, languish on a waiting list。

noteKo.exampleTr: 수천 명의 환자가 몇 달 동안 대기 명단에서 기다리고 있다.
noteKo.usage: in/on과 함께 쓰임: languish in prison, languish on a waiting list.

later.ex: We can talk about it later.

law.ex: Wearing a seat belt is the law.

legal.ex: What is the legal age to drive?

lists.en: written records of names in order
lists.ex: Write your name on the list.

maintained.ex: He maintains that the plan will work.

makes.ex: The company makes software for schools.

making.ex: The new law is making smoking illegal indoors.

many.ex: Many people work from home now.

mcglacken-byrne.ja: マクグラッケン＝バーン（姓）

mere.ex: The tickets sold out in a mere ten minutes.

million.ex: The city has over one million people.

mixed.en: combined so they are not separate
mixed.ex: Mix the flour and sugar together.

money.ex: They saved money for a new car.

moreover.ex: The flat is cheap; moreover, it is near the station.

necessity.ex: A car is a necessity in the countryside.

nevertheless.ex: It was raining; nevertheless, we went out.

noted.ex: She noted that prices were falling.

noting.en: mentioning or pointing out a fact
noting.ex: She spoke, noting that prices had risen.

number.ex: The number of tourists is rising.

observed.ex: She observed that the room was very quiet.

off.ex: All her hard work finally paid off.

on.en: used in 'pass on' = give to someone else
on.ex: Please pass the message on to your sister.

out.ex: He pointed out a mistake in my essay.

overlap.en: the part where two things cover the same area
overlap.ex: There is some overlap between the two courses.

parts.ex: Some parts of the film were boring.

passed.ex: Her grandfather passed away last year.

patients.ex: The nurse looked after ten patients.

pay.ex: I will pay for dinner tonight.

perceives.en: sees or thinks of something in a certain way
perceives.ex: He perceives exercise as a waste of time.

plastic.ex: We sat on plastic chairs in the garden.

pointing.ex: She explained her view, pointing to recent data.

policy.ex: The new housing policy starts in May.

population.en: all the people living in a place
population.ex: The population of Dublin is growing.

practice.en: what really happens, not just in theory
practice.ex: The idea is good, but it fails in practice.

presented.en: formally given or shown to a group
presented.ex: The report was presented to the board on Monday.

prevalent.en: common and happening in many places
prevalent.ex: The disease is prevalent in tropical areas.

example.en: Obesity is increasingly prevalent among children.
example.zh: 肥胖在兒童中越來越普遍。

note.usage: 多用於疾病、問題、觀念等，常見 be prevalent in/among；名詞 prevalence。

noteEn.meaning: Common and found in many places or people.
noteEn.usage: Often 'prevalent in/among'; used for diseases and problems.

paragraphs: A group of doctors spoke to politicians on Thursday. They said Ireland's health system has big problems.
More than one million people are waiting to see a hospital doctor. Many patients still wait on trolleys or in plastic chairs.
About half of Irish people think they need private health insurance. Not everyone can see a family doctor for free.
In 2017, Ireland agreed a plan called Sláintecare. It wanted good health care for everyone. Some parts worked, but many did not.
The doctors want more money for hospitals and family doctors. They say health care should be a right for everyone.
Ireland still does not have health care for everyone, a doctors' group told the Oireachtas health committee on Thursday.

Dr Domhnall McGlacken-Byrne, from Doctors for Universal Healthcare, said the size of the waiting lists is shocking. Earlier this year, the number of people waiting for hospital care went over one million. Patients still often wait on trolleys or in plastic chairs.

He said about half of Irish people feel they must pay for private health insurance. The public and private systems are mixed together in a way that is complicated and unfair. Many people also cannot see a GP for free.

The Sláintecare plan, agreed in 2017, has had some good results, but many of its changes have stopped. Dr McGlacken-Byrne asked for more money for hospitals, GPs and prevention, and for a law that makes health care a right.
Sara Burke of Trinity College Dublin said Ireland is still far from a universal system. The committee chair, Padraig Rice, said reform costs money but will pay off later.
Ireland still lacks a universal healthcare system in either policy or practice, a doctors' group told the Oireachtas health committee on Thursday.

Dr Domhnall McGlacken-Byrne, co-founder of Doctors for Universal Healthcare, described the scale of the State's waiting lists as extraordinary. The number of people awaiting specialist hospital care passed one million earlier this year, and patients on trolleys and plastic chairs remain common.

He said roughly half the population feels it needs private health insurance, and that the overlap between public and private hospitals is complicated, inefficient and unfair. GP care is also not available to everyone free of charge.

The Sláintecare reform plan, adopted in 2017, has had some successes, but many of its reforms have stalled. Dr McGlacken-Byrne called for sustained investment in primary care, hospitals and prevention, and for legislation making universal healthcare a legal entitlement.

Sara Burke of Trinity College Dublin said the country remains a long way from a universal system. Committee chair Padraig Rice said the State must accept that reform costs money but pays off in the long run.
Ireland has yet to deliver universal healthcare in either policy or practice, the Oireachtas health committee heard on Thursday.

Dr Domhnall McGlacken-Byrne, co-founder of Doctors for Universal Healthcare, branded the system a cause for scandal, pointing out that the number of people awaiting specialist hospital treatment surpassed one million earlier this year. Patients languishing on trolleys and plastic chairs, he said, remain commonplace.

Around half the population, he noted, feels compelled to buy private health insurance, while the entanglement of public and private provision is convoluted, inefficient and inequitable. Free GP access, moreover, is still not universal.

Although Sláintecare, adopted in 2017, can claim some achievements, many of its flagship reforms have faltered. He urged sustained, targeted investment in primary care, acute hospitals and prevention, alongside legislation enshrining universal healthcare as an entitlement rather than a mere aspiration.
Sara Burke of Trinity College Dublin echoed his concerns, while committee chair Padraig Rice argued that the State must accept that reform requires upfront spending that will pay dividends in time.
Ireland has not yet established a universal healthcare system in either policy or practice, according to evidence presented to the Oireachtas health committee on Thursday.

Dr Domhnall McGlacken-Byrne, co-founder of Doctors for Universal Healthcare, characterised the scale of waiting lists as extraordinary, noting that the number of individuals awaiting specialist hospital care exceeded one million earlier this year. Furthermore, the practice of treating patients on trolleys and plastic chairs remains prevalent.

He observed that approximately half of the population perceives private health insurance as a necessity, and that the overlap between public and private provision is complex, inefficient and inequitable. In addition, access to free GP care has not been extended to the entire population.

Although the Sláintecare strategy, adopted in 2017, has achieved certain successes, numerous reforms have subsequently stalled. Consequently, he advocated substantial and sustained investment in primary care, acute services and prevention, together with legislation establishing universal healthcare as a statutory entitlement.

Sara Burke of Trinity College Dublin concurred that the country remains considerably distant from a universal system. Nevertheless, committee chair Padraig Rice maintained that reform, while costly in the short term, would ultimately prove beneficial.
